## 1. Datadog

### 1.1 Plan tiers & billing units (high‑level)

Datadog’s public docs describe pricing in terms of *product‑specific plans* and *billing units* without a single “bundle” page:

- Host‑based products (Infrastructure Monitoring, APM, Database Monitoring, etc.) are billed per host (or host‑hour) on either a “high watermark” or “sum of hours” basis. ([docs.datadoghq.com](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/billing/pricing/?utm_source=openai))  
- Other products are billed by data volume (e.g., spans, logs), executions (e.g., synthetics), or seats. ([docs.datadoghq.com](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/billing/pricing/?utm_source=openai))  

The **main Datadog pricing doc** explains host billing and mentions that list prices per product live on the main pricing site, but does not itself enumerate those list prices. ([docs.datadoghq.com](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/billing/pricing/?utm_source=openai))  

**Public plan names** (without prices) from Datadog docs include:

- Infrastructure Monitoring: Pro, Enterprise (host‑based) ([docs.datadoghq.com](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/billing/pricing/?utm_source=openai))  
- APM & Distributed Tracing: Pro / Enterprise (host‑based) ([docs.datadoghq.com](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/billing/pricing/?utm_source=openai))  
- Log Management: Ingested logs vs Indexed logs, archive & rehydrate, etc. (usage‑based) ([docs.datadoghq.com](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/billing/pricing/?utm_source=openai))  
- Other modules (RUM, Synthetics, CI Visibility, etc.) have their own SKUs but their list prices are not detailed in the docs pages above. ([docs.datadoghq.com](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/billing/pricing/?utm_source=openai))  

The public investor materials confirm that:

- Infrastructure and APM are *priced per host*.  
- Logs are priced “primarily per log events indexed and secondarily by events ingested.” ([investors.datadoghq.com](https://investors.datadoghq.com/static-files/32d768c2-d21a-431d-ae09-ece0c5f20b37?utm_source=openai))  

> **Important:** Datadog’s current, complete per‑SKU list price table is **not** exposed in one place in the docs I can access; several independent sites quote $/host and $/GB numbers, but those are *not* official Datadog publications and therefore I treat per‑unit list prices as *unavailable*.

#### Summary – Datadog plan tiers & units (from Datadog docs only)

| Product family | Example plan tiers (names only) | Billing unit (from Datadog docs) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Infrastructure Monitoring | Pro, Enterprise | Per host (host‑hour or 99th‑percentile host count) ([docs.datadoghq.com](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/billing/pricing/?utm_source=openai)) |
| APM & Distributed Tracing | Pro, Enterprise | Per host; spans billed by GB of ingested spans tied to APM host commitments ([docs.datadoghq.com](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/billing/pricing/?utm_source=openai)) |
| Logs | Standard indexing, Flex storage, etc. | Primarily per log events indexed, secondarily per ingested events ([investors.datadoghq.com](https://investors.datadoghq.com/static-files/32d768c2-d21a-431d-ae09-ece0c5f20b37?utm_source=openai)) |
| Other products (RUM, Synthetics, etc.) | Product‑specific SKUs | Product‑specific units (e.g., tests run, sessions, etc.) – details in individual product docs, not a consolidated pricing table ([docs.datadoghq.com](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/billing/pricing/?utm_source=openai)) |

### 1.2 Included usage allowances (from Datadog docs)

Datadog’s *Product Allotments* documentation describes how usage allowances are linked to commitments, but again does not show list prices: ([docs.datadoghq.com](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/billing/product_allotments/?utm_source=openai))  

- For APM Pro, there is a default **ingested spans allotment** proportional to APM hosts; the doc gives an explicit example:  
  - 5 APM Pro Hosts × 150 GB ingested spans/host/month = 750 GB ingested spans/month allowance. ([docs.datadoghq.com](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/billing/product_allotments/?utm_source=openai))  
- The same table notes that different products (Infra Pro/Enterprise, IoT, Serverless, etc.) drive default allotments for **custom metrics**, span volumes, etc., again without price. Any *numerical* allowance outside that example (e.g., free custom‑metrics counts, free logs GB, RUM sessions) for each plan is **not** given centrally in the docs I can see.

## 2. New Relic

New Relic’s public pricing is more centralized and much of it *is* published numerically.

### 2.1 Plan tiers & billing units

The main pricing page, **“Transparent Pricing – Start for Free”**, describes a unified pricing model with:

- **User‑based pricing** and **compute‑based pricing** as two primary commercial models.  
- **Telemetry‑based pricing** for data ingest. ([newrelic.com](https://newrelic.com/pricing?utm_source=openai))  

Key public elements:

- **Free tier**  
  - 100 GB of free data ingest per month. ([newrelic.com](https://newrelic.com/pricing?utm_source=openai))  
- **Core “Original Data” option vs “Data Plus” option**  
  - New Relic Original Data:  
    - 100 GB free ingest per month, then **$0.40/GB** beyond 100 GB. ([newrelic.com](https://newrelic.com/pricing?utm_source=openai))  
  - Data Plus:  
    - Same 100 GB free, then **$0.60/GB** beyond 100 GB. ([newrelic.com](https://newrelic.com/pricing?utm_source=openai))  
- **Users**  
  - You choose “a monthly price for each engineer to access 50+ observability capabilities, or a compute price that unlocks access for all users” – but the actual $/user figures are **not** listed in text on that page. ([newrelic.com](https://newrelic.com/pricing?utm_source=openai))  

New Relic’s **usage plan documentation** references list prices and notes a 1.15x multiplier for EU data region accounts, but again doesn’t print the base list‑price numbers in that doc. ([docs.newrelic.com](https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/licenses/license-information/usage-plans/new-relic-usage-plan/?utm_source=openai))  

So at a high level:

| Component | Plan / option names | Billing unit (public) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Data ingest – Original | Original Data | Per GB ingested beyond 100 GB/month free ([newrelic.com](https://newrelic.com/pricing?utm_source=openai)) |
| Data ingest – Data Plus | Data Plus | Per GB ingested beyond 100 GB/month free ([newrelic.com](https://newrelic.com/pricing?utm_source=openai)) |
| Users | (Standard, Enterprise etc., names vary by edition; not fully enumerated on the main pricing page) | Per user per month (engineer) or per compute/host under compute model ([newrelic.com](https://newrelic.com/pricing?utm_source=openai)) |

### 2.2 List prices, included usage & overage (publicly stated)

From **newrelic.com/pricing**: ([newrelic.com](https://newrelic.com/pricing?utm_source=openai))  

- **Data ingest (Original Data):**  
  - Included: 100 GB free data ingest per month.  
  - Overage: **$0.40/GB** beyond the included 100 GB per month.  
  - Billing unit: GB per month.  

- **Data ingest (Data Plus):**  
  - Included: 100 GB free data ingest per month.  
  - Overage: **$0.60/GB** beyond the included 100 GB per month.

New Relic’s **Usage plan documentation** lists the concept of “list price” and notes that EU accounts multiply the list price by 1.15, but again doesn’t state the baseline list price or user‑tier dollar amounts; it defers to the main pricing page and your order. ([docs.newrelic.com](https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/licenses/license-information/usage-plans/new-relic-usage-plan/?utm_source=openai))
